title: Implement Medium class
description: Create python/src/lichen/sim/medium.py. Tracks active transmissions. Methods: start_tx(node_id, payload, tx_power) -> Transmission, get_rx_candidates(node_id, position, time) -> list of (Transmission, rssi, snr). Uses PropagationModel for path loss. Collision detection: find overlapping TXs. Capture effect: if strongest signal is 6+ dB above second strongest, it wins; otherwise all colliding packets lost. Configurable noise_floor_dbm (default -120). Unit tests for: single TX delivery, collision with both lost, capture effect winner.
notes: 2026-08-27 leaf audit: the active Medium implementation is owned by the pinned external lora-medium dependency at uv.lock commit 5ddc92bdda141b3f90920abbe0f259e84b37b211; project-LICHEN has no local sim/medium.py to patch. Focused pytest across test_medium, test_simulation, hidden-terminal, and jammer-interference passed 90 tests. Focused Ruff on test_medium and test_simulation passed; strict mypy exposes 28 existing test typing errors around Optional Transmission/TDMASlot and one state comparison. Direct runtime edge probes found unmet acceptance in the external class: Medium accepts NaN noise_floor_dbm; start_tx accepts negative time_us, list payloads instead of bytes, NaN positions, negative channel, unknown phy_mode, and negative frequency_hz. It also permits non-monotonic start insertion (a time-100 TX followed by time-0 remains stored as late, early), so monotonic scheduling/lifecycle invariants are unenforced. Node registration, RX timeout delivery, and deterministic event tie ordering live in local Simulation/EventQueue rather than Medium and their focused tests passed, but fixing the Medium input/lifecycle gaps requires changing and releasing lora-medium then repinning LICHEN. No files modified for this bead; claim released.
close_reason: Wave 3 complete. 241 tests pass, ruff clean.
